papers.title: Cosmological constraints on single-field inflation models from ACT/SPT data and observations at sub-Mpc scales
papers.abstract: We investigate single-field inflation models that can produce large curvature perturbations at sub-Mpc scales while remaining consistent with cosmological observations across multiple regimes. We highlight the tension between generating enhanced small-scale perturbations and maintaining agreement with the scalar spectral index $n_s$ measured by ACT and SPT, which disfavors several conventional single-field inflation models. To address this issue, we propose three viable classes of inflationary potentials: bump/dip-modified, step-like, and double-inflection-point. Each can sufficiently amplify primordial perturbations while predicting $n_s$ that lie within the $2σ$ range of current observational bounds. In addition, we examine the primordial power spectra predicted by these models and constrain their parameter spaces using cosmological observations at different scales, including CMB, BAO, PBH, PTA, and CMB-distortion. Our results show that some of the models considered can simultaneously satisfy the ACT/SPT constraints and account for the current PTA observations, although doing so while respecting the constraints on the PBH abundance remains challenging.
papers.ai_summary: We investigate single-field inflation models that can produce large curvature perturbations at sub-Mpc scales while remaining consistent with cosmological observations across multiple regimes.

papers.title: A Collimated Protostellar Outflow Likely Driven by Jet and Reshaped by Environment in the Sagittarius C Cloud of the Central Molecular Zone
papers.abstract: The Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) at the center of the Galaxy provides a nearby laboratory for studying star formation under extreme physical and chemical conditions. Recent ALMA (Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array) observations have identified 43 candidate protostellar outflows in three CMZ clouds. One of these, the Sgr C-F#2 outflow in Sagittarius C (Sgr C), has a highly collimated lobe extending approximately 0.8 pc in projection. Here we present a joint analysis of ALMA observations of SiO J=8-7, 5-4, and 2-1. We use local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) and non-LTE methods to constrain the SiO column densities, H2 number density, and gas temperature. The low SiO rotational temperatures and higher kinetic temperatures inferred from non-LTE methods suggest subthermal excitation. The elongated SiO morphology, shock-excited gas, position-velocity structure, and the alignment of the red shifted molecular lobe with JWST infrared knots altogether favor jet-dominated entrainment, whereas a broader disk-wind component close to the source cannot be excluded. The outflow shows asymmetries in its morphology and physical properties, which can be attributed to dense gas on the path of its lobe impeding its propagation and feedback from a nearby HII region imposing different pressure on its two sides.
papers.ai_summary: The Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) at the center of the Galaxy provides a nearby laboratory for studying star formation under extreme physical and chemical conditions.

papers.title: Periodic radio emission from a rapidly rotating T8 ultracool dwarf
papers.abstract: We report the discovery of periodic radio bursts from the T8 brown dwarf WISE J151721.13+052929.3 (WISE J1517+05), detected with ASKAP and MeerKAT. The emission is characterised by a stable periodicity of $1.149 \pm 0.002$ hr, placing WISE J1517+05 among the fastest rotating radio-detected ultracool dwarfs (UCDs). The radio bursts are broadband and highly variable, reaching a peak spectral luminosity of $L_ν = 5.6 \times 10^{15}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,Hz^{-1}}$, making WISE J1517+05 the brightest periodic UCD to date. The high brightness temperature of the radio bursts ($T_B>10^{11}$ K), combined with the rotational modulation, strongly favour an auroral electron cyclotron maser emission (ECME) origin. In contrast to most known radio-bursting UCDs, the bursts exhibit relatively low and variable circular polarisation fractions (typically $\sim 20\%$). These properties suggest significant depolarisation of intrinsically highly polarised ECME, likely due to propagation effects in a structured magnetospheric plasma. Notably, we also observe a polarisation reversal within a single burst profile, which is currently unexplained. We model the emission using a dipolar magnetic field with emission arising from a single active field line, and find a moderate inclination angle of $i = 47.9^{+11.4}_{-9.2}$ degrees and a magnetic obliquity of $β= 40.1^{+9.2}_{-10.9}$ degrees. WISE J1517+05 expands the parameter space of radio-active UCDs toward higher luminosities and lower polarisation fractions, suggesting that current surveys may be sensitive to a larger population than previously recognised, while searches relying on methods that assume high circular polarisation fractions risk missing a subset of UCDs. More broadly, this discovery reinforces the idea that rapid rotation plays a key role in generating strong dipolar magnetic fields in UCDs that can give rise to auroral radio emission.
papers.ai_summary: We report the discovery of periodic radio bursts from the T8 brown dwarf WISE J151721.13+052929.3 (WISE J1517+05), detected with ASKAP and MeerKAT.

papers.title: Does the Escape Fraction Prescription Shape Reionization History and Morphology?
papers.abstract: The escape fraction of ionizing photons, $f_{\rm esc}$, is one of the least constrained quantities of the Epoch of Reionization (EoR), and the opacity of the intergalactic medium prevents its direct measurement at high redshifts. We constrain three power-law parameterizations, $f_{\rm esc}(z)$, $f_{\rm esc}(M_{\rm h})$, and $f_{\rm esc}(z, M_{\rm h})$, against JWST UV luminosity functions and EoR observables (the ionizing emissivity, the neutral hydrogen fraction, and the Thomson optical depth) using Markov Chain Monte Carlo, with priors that allow $f_{\rm esc}$ to either increase or decrease with redshift and halo mass. We then propagate the best-fit models into the semi-numerical simulation SimFast21 and compare their ionization morphology and 21 cm power spectra with those of a constant-$f_{\rm esc}$ model. All models reproduce the observations with nearly identical global reionization histories. The data favor an escape fraction that decreases with increasing redshift, from $\approx 0.8$ at $z = 5$ to $\approx 0.35$ at $z = 15$. The halo-mass-only model prefers $f_{\rm esc}$ increasing with halo mass, but this trend acts as a proxy for redshift evolution. When we vary both dependencies jointly, the data prefer a mass-independent $f_{\rm esc}$. At matched global neutral fraction, the ionization morphology is closely similar for all four prescriptions, and the 21 cm power spectra agree to within $\approx 10\%$. These results suggest that, once calibrated against the same observations, the details of the $f_{\rm esc}$ prescription, which are set by the physics of the interstellar medium, largely average out in both the global observables and the 21 cm power spectrum. Distinguishing them may require statistics beyond the power spectrum, such as sightline statistics of the Ly$α$ and 21 cm forests, or forecasts that exploit their small differences in reionization timing.

papers.title: Classification of Fermi Blazars of Uncertain Type Using Positive-Unlabelled Machine Learning
papers.abstract: We apply positive-unlabelled (PU) machine learning to the 1623 blazars of uncertain type (BCUs) in the Fermi Large Area Telescope Fourth Source Catalogue, Data Release 4 (4FGL-DR4). Five PU classifiers are trained on seven gamma-ray features, once with the 820 flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs) and once with the 1490 BL Lac objects as the labelled class (FSRQ mode and BL Lac mode). Each source is scored out of fold over 100 repeated five-fold splits, and its confidence is the fraction of splits in which at least three of the five classifiers flag it. At a confidence of at least 0.1, 437 BCUs are FSRQ-like, 597 are BL Lac-like, 12 are flagged in both modes and 577 in neither. On known sources the ensemble reaches a recall of 0.80 in FSRQ mode and 0.82 in BL Lac mode at a false-positive rate of 0.08, but a logistic regression trained on the labelled sources alone does at least as well, so PU learning gives no accuracy gain here. Removing the sky coordinates from the features does not lower the performance on known sources but adds 107 BCUs to the candidate lists and drops 30, which is consistent with the coordinates acting as a selection shortcut, so we exclude them. We check the candidates against published optical spectra, SDSS-V spectra, and BCUs that later received a class in the catalogue. Among sources assigned a single class, BL Lac-like calls are correct for 84 to 100% of the sources and FSRQ-like calls for 58 to 83%, depending on the sample. These samples come from spectroscopic follow-up and do not represent all BCUs. The candidates are fainter and lie closer to the Galactic plane than the labelled sources, and the excess of unclassified BCUs in the plane is not explained. We release the confidences of all 1623 BCUs.

papers.title: Improving cosmological distance measurements at high redshift using Lyman-Alpha forest BAO reconstruction
papers.abstract: The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) measures baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) in the Lyman-$α$ (Lyman-alpha) forest and provides a robust probe of the expansion history in the matter-dominated era. Yet, non-linear structure formation broadens and shifts the BAO peak. To undo these effects, we extend standard Zel'dovich reconstruction, routinely applied to galaxy surveys, to the Lyman-alpha forest. We validate our methodology on large-volume idealized Lyman-alpha forest mocks painted on top of the \textsc{AbacusSummit} $N$-body simulations, using linear control variates to suppress sample variance and thereby reduce the error bars by a factor of up to $\approx \sqrt{50}$. In fully sampled periodic boxes, reconstruction halves the radial BAO damping scale and reduces the uncertainties on the radial ($\apar$) and transverse ($\aperp$) scaling parameters by $\approx25\%$ and $\approx15\%$, respectively. It also reduces the non-linear shift from $Δ\apar=+0.3\%$ to $+0.10\pm0.07\%$, while $\aperp$ remains unbiased. To make this approach readily applicable to observational data, we demonstrate the impact of a survey mask with a DESI-like density of $50\,\mathrm{deg}^{-2}$. For this mask, we compare two approaches to estimate the displacement field: either directly from the Lyman-alpha forest or using an external tracer with a number density of $\bar n \simeq 10^{-3}\,h^3\mathrm{Mpc}^{-3}$, such as Lyman-break galaxies and Lyman-$α$ emitters---both key targets for DESI-II. Both approaches give comparable gains and reduce the uncertainties on $\apar$ and $\aperp$ by $\approx 27\%$ and $\approx 10\%$, respectively, with mild improvements for futuristic high-density surveys with $160\,\mathrm{deg}^{-2}$. Correspondingly, the figure of merit improves by factors of $1.66$ for fully sampled boxes, $1.65$ for a DESI-like, and $1.76$ for a high-density survey.

papers.title: Measuring the magnetization profiles of galaxy groups and clusters
papers.abstract: Magnetic fields are vital in determining the physical conditions of baryons in massive halos. They are, however, notoriously difficult to observe. This impacts problems from our understanding of galaxy formation, to the observed deficit in the amplitude of thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ) power spectrum that affects cosmological inferences. Although Faraday rotation measures (RMs) offer a direct probe of magnetic fields, it weights magnetic fields by the free-electron density. Several probes of free electrons, including fast radio burst (FRB) dispersion measures (DMs) and kinematic SZ (kSZ) effect, are now maturing into precision tools. We combine RM$^2$ stacks from SPICE-RACS around DESI galaxy groups and ROSAT clusters with optical depth profiles constrained jointly by the FRB DM-redshift relation and the kSZ effect, and obtain 95% upper limits on the rms line-of-sight magnetic field of $<3.9$-$11.6~μ$G ($<2.3$-$6.4~μ$G) in groups (clusters) for a 10~kpc coherence length. Combining these with thermal pressure profiles inferred from tSZ-shear cross-correlations, we obtain 95% lower limits on the plasma $β$ of $>0.31$ ($>11$) in groups (clusters). Although current constraints are only limits, we forecast a first detection with larger datasets from the Deep Synoptic Array (DSA). We present the first forecast of the DSA RM grid density ($\sim365$ RMs deg$^{-2}$), which when combined with 10$^4$ FRBs would measure the field in groups to $3$-$13\%$ precision, compared to current constraints of $38$-$75\%$. Although the interpretation of current measurements remains challenging owing to depolarization along turbulent halo sightlines and the unknown coherence length, larger samples and DSA/Square Kilometer Array observations may resolve these uncertainties by measuring polarization-fraction profiles and the RM structure function using extended radio sources, respectively.
papers.ai_summary: This impacts problems from our understanding of galaxy formation, to the observed deficit in the amplitude of thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ) power spectrum that affects cosmological inferences.

papers.title: Getting Ready For Analysing Rubin Data : CLMM v2, The Updated LSST-DESC Cluster Weak Lensing Mass Modeling Library For Cosmology
papers.abstract: The Dark Energy Science Collaboration has prepared a multitude of pipelines to process the upcoming Vera C. Rubin Observatory data and perform different scientific analyses. Here, we present the methodology to constrain the mass information of galaxy clusters from weak lensing, which is encompassed by the v2.0 release of the Cluster Lensing Mass Modeling (CLMM) code. This Python library provides the ingredients for both the modeling and data reduction of lensing observables, and the improvements in the new version were customized to handle the first WL analyses of LSST clusters, including, e.g., stacking functionalities and WL multipoles. This new version of CLMM has allowed various cluster analyses using LSST-DESC simulated data, precursor survey and Rubin commissioning and survey validation data, and is ready to be used for the first cluster cosmology analyses. CLMM is an open-source software package collaboratively written in Python, providing multiple example notebooks, including a set that can reproduce all figures in this work, and extensive documentation, publicly available at https://lsstdesc.org/CLMM/.

papers.title: A Hierarchical Bayesian Differential Calibration of the Gaia DR3 Parallax Zero Point Using Galactic Globular Clusters
papers.abstract: Globular clusters (GCs) occupy a broad range of stellar colors and magnitudes while sharing nearly the same distance. Gaia Data Release 3 parallaxes retain systematic zero-point residual variations for GCs, even after the correction by the widely used standard correction model (L21). We derive an empirical residual correction by the Hierarchical Bayesian Model, separating cluster-level offsets from the differential information carried by the member sequences. We first evaluate the L21 baseline at a fixed reference color, which assigns the remaining color-dependent correction to the residual model. Then we model the residual zero point, $δZ(G,ν_{\rm eff})$, with B-splines functions in color and magnitude--color interaction terms. The uncorrected cluster residuals exhibit a negative offset of approximately $25$--$40~μ{\rm as}$. The L21 baseline removes most of this offset but leaves coherent color- and magnitude-dependent structure. Applying the residual model brings the mean residuals close to zero, especially across most of the sampled color range. In five-fold cross-validation that excludes entire clusters from training, the correction modestly reduces the magnitude- and color-trend RMS relative to the L21 correction. The resulting model therefore provides a differential refinement of the \textit{Gaia} DR3 parallax zero-point within the calibrated domain for GCs, rather than an independent determination of its absolute value.
papers.ai_summary: We derive an empirical residual correction by the Hierarchical Bayesian Model, separating cluster-level offsets from the differential information carried by the member sequences.

papers.title: Late reheating in the era of precision cosmology
papers.abstract: We study the minimum cosmic reheating temperature allowed by recent measurements of primordial nuclear abundances and of the cosmic microwave background. We find that reheating by decays of a light particle into electrons and neutrinos is compatible with both at temperatures around 0.4 MeV, an order of magnitude below the bound for purely electromagnetic channels. This scenario has implications for cosmology and laboratory searches. For example, nearly standard neutrino radiation can coexist with a smaller active neutrino mass density at unchanged physical masses, by up to a factor of five for normal ordering. The weaker suppression of clustering changes matter power at the percent level, which forthcoming galaxy surveys and lensing measurements may probe. Late reheating also suppresses sterile neutrino production at mixings within the projected reach of laboratory experiments.
papers.ai_summary: This scenario has implications for cosmology and laboratory searches.

papers.title: X-ray Emission Study of TeV Blazars
papers.abstract: In this work, we present a systematic X-ray study of 85 TeV-detected blazars based on archival \emph{Swift}-XRT and \emph{NuSTAR} observations available up to May 2024. We derive unabsorbed X-ray fluxes and photon indices through spectral fitting, and investigate their light curves, spectral energy distributions, flux distributions, power spectral densities, and flux-index correlations. Using the fractional variability method, we identify 78 sources as variable in the soft X-ray band and 14 sources as variable in the hard X-ray band. For well-sampled soft X-ray light curves, the flux distributions are generally better described by log-normal functions, while the PSD slopes span $β_{\rm PSD}=0.1$--$1.6$, with most values between 1.0 and 1.6, where the PSD is defined as $P(f)\propto f^{-β_{\rm PSD}}$. We find positive correlations between TeV and X-ray luminosities, supporting a leptonic emission scenario. We also find a correlation between X-ray and disk luminosities, whereas no significant correlation is found between X-ray luminosity and black hole mass.

papers.title: A Quiet Night in the Millihertz Sky? LISA Forecasts from LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA Populations
papers.abstract: The high-mass black hole population inferred from ground-based observations can substantially affect the number of binaries detectable by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). We use population constraints based on data from the latest LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog (GWTC-5.0), as well as constraints from the O3 search for intermediate-mass black hole binaries, to forecast the number and masses of binary black holes detectable by LISA. Using the released GWTC-5.0 population posterior, we obtain $6.6^{+5.5}_{-2.2}$ expected detections with signal-to-noise ratio $>8$ in 4 years (median and $90\%$ credible interval). The alternative population models we consider use a broken power law with two or three Gaussian peaks for either the primary-mass distribution or a common mass distribution for both black holes. For the three-peak model with the common mass distribution, extrapolating from $300$ to $1000M_\odot$ roughly doubles the median expected number of LISA detections to $\sim14$. The upper end of its $90\%$ credible interval rises from tens to thousands of expected detections, although approximations may limit the reliability of the most extreme counts. For the reference GWTC-5.0 population, $39^{+22}_{-11}\%$ of the binaries detectable by LISA merge during the mission or within $10$ years after its end and are potential multiband sources. Essentially all of these mergers would be detectable by a reference Cosmic Explorer configuration if it is operating at merger. Ground-based measurements of the high-mass population can therefore inform both LISA forecasts and the prospects for observing the same binaries through inspiral and merger.

papers.title: Effects of Dust in Electron-Capture Supernovae: Difficulty in Explaining Intermediate Luminosity Red Transients
papers.abstract: The progenitors of intermediate-luminosity red transients (ILRTs) spanning the luminosity gap between novae and supernovae are under debate, and electron-capture supernovae (ECSNe) have been proposed as a strong candidate. ECSNe from super asymptotic giant branch (super-AGB) stars have been theoretically predicted to be much brighter than ILRTs, but attenuation by dusty winds of their super-AGB progenitors may ease this tension. Here we construct a semi-analytical framework for calculating the light curves of ECSNe with dust attenuation and re-emission, by combining recent ECSN light curve predictions with a model for dust physics. Even by varying both the wind mass-loss rate and the ECSN model parameters, we find it challenging to simultaneously fit the light curve and color evolution of ILRTs. This poses a potential challenge to the standard models of ECSNe for explaining ILRTs. For explaining ILRTs, we propose either the existence of a population of ECSNe with much lower explosion energies ($\sim$10$^{48}$-$10^{49}$ erg) and dimmer plateaus, or alternative model(s) to ECSNe that realize such low explosion energies.

papers.title: Rare Blue-core BCGs as Optical Signatures of ICM Cooling
papers.abstract: Blue cores in brightest cluster galaxies (BCGs) trace recent central activity associated with cooling cluster atmospheres. We search for blue cores at $z<0.6$ in five eROSITA all-sky surveys using X-ray data, optical imaging, and optical spectroscopy. We identify 379 blue-core BCGs among 11352 systems (3.3%), although contamination increases toward higher redshift. Of these, 98 (0.86%) are X-ray bright. Their defining signature is a central $g-r$ color at least 0.2 mag bluer than the reference population within $a=20$ kpc before returning to the normal BCG envelope. Ha emission equivalent width correlates strongly with the blue continuum excess, consistent with young stellar components comprising ~0.1-1% of pre-existing stellar mass. Line ratios indicate widespread LINER-like excitation, with a larger star-forming contribution in blue Ha emitters but substantial non-stellar excitation. This activity is closely linked to the thermodynamics of the host-cluster gas. At $0.1R_{500}$, cooling times decrease from BCGs without significant Ha emission to red and then blue Ha emitters. Blue BCGs preferentially occur in clusters with $L_{\rm X,300}>10^{44}$ erg s$^{-1}$; red Ha emitters also favor higher X-ray luminosities. The blue-core fraction rises with optical richness. For systems with $t_{\rm cool}(0.1R_{500})<20$ Gyr, doubling richness increases the odds of hosting a blue-core BCG by $2.45\pm0.39$. This indicates that cluster scale carries information beyond cooling time, plausibly through the amount of gas available for cooling and condensation. The scarcity of blue BCGs without significant Ha emission disfavors isolated short bursts followed by long Ha-quiet fading phases. It can instead be explained by sustained or closely recurrent star formation over timescales much longer than 100 Myr, or by Ha persisting through additional excitation mechanisms as the young stellar component fades.

papers.title: Revealing the companion of NGC 1850-BH1
papers.abstract: The nature of the system NGC 1850-BH1 is discussed controversially in the literature. Located in the young (100 Myr) massive cluster NGC 1850 in the Large Magellanic Cloud, it was initially proposed to consist of a 5 $M_\odot$ main sequence turn-off star orbiting a stellar-mass black hole. However, subsequent analyses of the system have presented an alternative explanation, comprising of a lower mass (1-2 $M_\odot$) puffed-up donor star orbiting a rapidly rotating mass accretor. Efforts to discern the secondary's nature as a luminous star or a compact object in the original spectroscopy have remained inconclusive. In this work, we analyse a set of follow-up multi-epoch FLAMES-ARGUS spectra, which are bluer and of higher spectral resolution than the original data. Exploiting the spectral disentangling technique, we reveal the luminous secondary, and constrain the parameters of both components. We can describe the system self-consistently, adopting a 1.7 $\pm$ 0.4 $M_\odot$ puffed-up mass donor and a rapidly rotating ($v\sin{i} = 275$ km/s) 5.2 $\pm$ 2.6 $M_\odot$ luminous companion. While this rules out the black hole hypothesis, tensions with the analysis of the original data remain: Our inferred flux ratio of $\sim$ 35-50% in the red optical wavelength range is higher than the 10% upper limit found in previous work. The origin of this discrepancy remains unclear. Thanks to its location in a cluster of well-known mass and metallicity and its peculiar orbital properties, NGC 1850-BH1 has the potential to serve as a benchmark for mass-transfer efficiency studies.

papers.title: Three-flavor neutrino Boltzmann transport and flavor instabilities in long-lived neutron-star merger remnants
papers.abstract: Binary neutron-star (BNS) mergers are multimessenger sources whose kilonova emission and nucleosynthesis depend sensitively on neutrino microphysics and flavor conversion. Most BNS merger simulations assume $μ$-$τ$ neutrino degeneracy in a two-flavor treatment. We investigate the fast flavor instability (FFI) and the collisional flavor instability (CFI) in long-lived BNS merger remnants using axisymmetric general-relativistic three-flavor Boltzmann neutrino transport with a comprehensive treatment of muons and muonic interactions, following a handoff from 3D grey moment-based simulations. Our simulations largely reproduce the parent 3D simulations, recovering trapped weak equilibrium in the core, muonic non-equilibrium in the semitransparent outer disk due to prolonged demuonization, and cold weak equilibrium in transparent regions. Linear stability analysis reveals strong and widespread CFI in all three flavor sectors, including narrow resonance-like structures. Muonic interactions reshape the FFI distribution, shifting the $eτ$-sector instability toward denser disk regions compared with the extended FFI outside the disk in the two-flavor model, while disk demuonization produces a strong $ν_μ$ excess and one-sided muon-lepton-number angular distributions that suppress FFI in the $eμ$ and $μτ$ sectors. Local three-flavor quantum kinetic equation (QKE) calculations reveal nonlinear coupling among flavor sectors that excites coherence even in an initially stable sector. Diagonal collisional repopulation is decisive for the nonlinear evolution and asymptotic flavor populations, and neglecting it overestimates flavor equilibration. We establish the necessity of three-flavor transport from both classical and quantum perspectives, and underscore the importance of consistently coupling flavor conversion with diagonal collisional repopulation in future CFI subgrid models.

papers.title: A gaussian-process reconstruction of gravitational-wave friction from dark standard sirens
papers.abstract: Standard sirens provide a direct probe of the cosmic distance-redshift relation and therefore a powerful test of whether gravitational waves (GWs) propagate as predicted by general relativity on cosmological scales. In many extensions of general relativity, GW propagation is modified by an anomalous friction term, which alters the amplitude evolution and leads to a GW luminosity distance that differs from its electromagnetic counterpart. In this work, we develop a non-parametric reconstruction of this anomalous friction from dark standard sirens. We reconstruct its redshift dependence, encoded in the friction function $α_M(z)$, with a Gaussian process (GP) and derive the corresponding GW-to-EM luminosity-distance ratio $Ξ(z)$ by integration, explicitly retaining the relation between the local friction modification and its accumulated effect on the observed distance, while enforcing a monotonic and invertible GW luminosity distance. We apply the method to the GWTC-5.0 catalog, jointly inferring the source population, modified propagation, and background cosmological parameters. We find no evidence for departures from GR, with $α_M=0$ and $Ξ=1$ consistent with the posterior over the redshift range probed by the catalog. The result is stable under variations of the GP kernel, smoothness and amplitude priors, resolution prescription, and likelihood treatment. We further introduce function-space diagnostics for comparing flexible and parametric reconstructions, including prior calibration, prior-to-posterior contraction, common summaries of propagation-population degeneracies, and principal-component analysis. These tools make explicit which features are informed by the data and which are imposed by the function-space prior, providing a framework for interpretable non-parametric tests of gravitational-wave propagation.

papers.title: ECH0EZ: Estimating the Hubble constant with ZTF SN Ia DR2
papers.abstract: Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) are instrumental for a precise measurement of the Hubble constant ($H_0$) from the local distance ladder, yet the data used hitherto for this purpose are inhomogeneous and subject to severe selection effects. We present the first, preliminary, cosmological analysis of 772 SNe Ia from the Zwicky Transient Facility's second data release: an untargeted single-telescope sample whose volume-limited subset (z<0.06) is largely free of Malmquist bias. We correct the public data for known instrumental and calibration biases and the redshifts for peculiar motions. Using the 42 SH0ES calibrators (their host distances computed from Cepheids and geometric anchors) and a Bayesian hierarchical model of SN Ia standardisation, dust extinction, redshift and calibration uncertainties, we infer $H_0 = (71.6 \pm 1.5)$ km/s/Mpc after marginalising over deceleration with a flat prior (or $(72.3 \pm 1.1)$ km/s/Mpc if a prior on matter density from Pantheon+ is imposed), with the uncertainty dominated by the number of calibrators. We demonstrate robustness to the choice of light-curve and Milky Way dust models and to extensions of the model to include peculiar-velocity correlations, a host-mass step, and two stretch populations. These results are in agreement with previous distance-ladder measurements and $2.7σ$ ($4.1σ$) away from the value obtained from Planck data, suggesting that the resolution of the Hubble tension lies outside of SNe Ia---or the distance ladder entirely.

papers.title: Can inflationary axion fluctuations dominate over misalignment?
papers.abstract: The relic abundance of light stable axion dark matter is usually set by misalignment. We study whether the inflationary fluctuations of the axion can dominate instead, and we follow the modes analytically through an instantaneous transition from de Sitter expansion to radiation domination, neglecting the axion mass during inflation and keeping it afterward. Since the energy density is quadratic in the field, a fluctuation-dominated abundance carries an isocurvature perturbation even when the mean displacement vanishes. For a canonical minimally coupled axion the spectrum is scale invariant, and fluctuation-dominated dark matter exceeds the Planck isocurvature limit by about eight orders of magnitude. An inflaton-dependent kinetic function or a nonminimal coupling to the Ricci scalar tilts the spectrum blue, moving the fluctuation power from CMB scales to small scales. Imposing the Planck limit at the pivot scale, we find that fluctuation-dominated dark matter with a constant kinetic slope requires the spectral tilt $n_η-1\gtrsim0.27$ and the axion mass $m_η \gtrsim200 \rm{GeV}$ at $H_I=10^{10}\rm{GeV}$, and $n_η-1\gtrsim0.34$ and $m_η\gtrsim4.5\,$keV at $H_I=10^{13}\rm{GeV}$. A kinetic function with a running slope lowers these masses to $1.4~\rm{GeV}$ and $0.7\,$eV, respectively. For the QCD axion, whose oscillations start late, we estimate that any single power-law spectrum blue enough to satisfy the pivot limit gives too little fluctuation abundance, and misalignment dominates.

papers.title: Impact of Neutrino Trapping on the Equation of State and Structure of Hybrid Stars with 2SC Quark Matter
papers.abstract: We investigate how sensitive the effects of neutrino trapping on hot hybrid stars are to uncertainties in the hadronic and quark equations of state and in the thermodynamic construction of the hadron--quark transition. The hadronic phase is described by finite-temperature covariant density functional equations of state, and the quark phase by a three-flavor Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model with repulsive vector interactions and two-flavor color superconductivity. Because confinement is absent from the NJL model, an effective pressure shift $B^*$ is used phenomenologically to locate the deconfinement transition. We construct isentropic stellar equations of state with and without trapped electron neutrinos, vary the quark vector coupling and the nuclear symmetry-energy slope, and compare global with local conservation of electron-lepton number within phase coexistence. Neutrino trapping generically shifts deconfinement toward higher density throughout the parameter range considered. Increasing the vector interaction stiffens quark matter and raises the maximum stellar mass, but only moderately for the couplings studied. We also examine stronger diquark pairing and RG-consistent regularization, instead of sharp momentum cut-off: both affect the pairing gap, phase boundaries, and quark-core composition more strongly than they alter the qualitative trends of the stellar mass--radius sequences. Conversely, trapping reduces the sensitivity to the hadronic symmetry-energy slope because the enhanced proton fraction drives matter toward greater isospin symmetry. Global and local lepton-number prescriptions produce rather similar mass--radius relations but substantially different internal phase structures: global conservation leads to a considerably more extended mixed phase.

papers.title: The Great Chat in the Sky: Aligning Exotic Astronomical Data to Language with AstroBridge
papers.abstract: Astronomical observations include images, spectra, and light curves, while the scientific literature describes these objects in natural language. We present AstroBridge, a framework that connects these observations to an LLM through a literature-assisted caption generation pipeline. We used catalog metadata to match observations with scientific texts that describe the same objects. A vision-language model generates descriptive captions from representations of observations, matched passages, and available metadata, creating observation-caption pairs without manual captioning. We train AstroBridge to predict captions directly from raw observations. Modality-specific frozen encoders extract representations that a shared, trainable fusion network aligns with the embedding space of an LLM. In caption-based evaluation of spectra, AstroBridge achieves 91.5% accuracy in distinguishing quasars from galaxies, compared to 69.0% from the base model prior to fine-tuning. Limitations remain in galaxy morphology, classification of minority supernova classes, and the factual quality of generated captions. We believe that AstroBridge's framework is a step towards the goal of aligning the totality of astronomy's diverse, exotic data through the lingua franca of text.

papers.title: Measuring masses of transiting Earth-like planets: first insights from the PLATO RV data challenge
papers.abstract: The PLATO Stellar Variability Mitigation Working Group designed a radial-velocity (RV) data challenge to assess the precision and accuracy achievable on RV semi-amplitudes in the context of the future PLATO follow-up. Using Sun-as-a-star observations obtained with HARPS-N, we generated three multi-planet systems with realistic sampling, an effective signal-to-noise ratio of S/N ~ 450, an exposure time of 15 minutes, and a total of approximately 1000 observations. The resulting data set is publicly available and can serve as a benchmark for the community to test and compare RV analysis methods. Eight independent teams participated in the challenge, aiming to recover the semi-amplitudes of both transiting and non-transiting planets. A meta-analysis of the submitted results shows that, with current data analysis methods, HARPS-N-like stability and the observing strategy studied in this paper, achieving a precision on semi-amplitudes better than 10% for habitable-zone signals around a solar-type star is challenging, and is typically limited to planets with masses of approximately 8-10 Earth masses. This performance is expected to improve for K dwarfs, where planets down to approximately 2-5 Earth masses may be characterized at a similar level of precision. Finally, based on the results of this challenge and the occurrence of false positives, we derive an empirical detection threshold for RV surveys, which can be used to distinguish robust planetary detections from candidates.
authors: for the PLATO Stellar Variability Working Group

papers.title: On the Interpretation of Tests of the Horizon Area Law
papers.abstract: This Letter investigates gravitational-wave tests of the horizon area law. Although they provide a striking consistency check of general relativity (GR), these tests rely on models that assume GR, making their interpretation inherently model dependent. We show with a specific example---simulations of merging boson stars---that exotic compact objects can mimic merging black holes and pass an area-law test at a confidence as high as $\sim 92\%$ despite not even having event horizons.

papers.title: Asymmetric Reheating of a Dark Sector
papers.abstract: We study asymmetric post-inflationary reheating in a framework with two sequestered MSSM-like sectors (the ``visible'' and ``dark'' sectors) with different supersymmetry-breaking scales, with dark matter corresponding to the lightest dark baryons. In this setup, independent Affleck-Dine dynamics in the two sectors offers a natural explanation for the comparable abundances of visible and dark matter. We relate the resulting temperature hierarchy to the inflaton's partial decay widths in different kinematical regimes, where it may decay into dark sector particles via 2-, 3- or 4-body processes. The latter case yields the most asymmetric reheating scenario, and we discuss the implications of this regime for the dark sector's thermal history, namely regarding the corresponding strong and weak interactions. While in this kinematical regime the contribution of light dark sector degrees of freedom to $ΔN_{\rm eff}$ is negligible, we show that it increases significantly in the regime where 3-body decays are possible, particularly near the threshold for dark Higgs pair-production where $ΔN_{\rm eff}^{\max} \simeq 0.078$. The current combined BBN+CMB+BAO bound leaves only a narrow allowed interval of the 2-body decay regime immediately above threshold, while next-generation CMB experiments could probe slightly below it.

papers.title: The Impact of Flyby Interactions on the Rotation of Open Clusters
papers.abstract: The Gaia astrometric mission has provided the first evidence for the bulk rotation of open clusters. While this rotation may arise from residual spin inherited from a cluster's parent molecular cloud, it is unclear whether this explanation always suffices, as angular momentum is carried away by escaping stars on the timescale of two-body relaxation. In particular, the recent observance of significant rotation ($v_{\rm rot} = 0.81 \pm 0.06$ km s$^{-1}$) in the dynamically old ($\approx 4$ Gyr) open cluster M67 motivates a study of another potential source of spin for Solar neighborhood clusters: tidal torquing from gravitational encounters with passing giant molecular clouds (GMCs). We derive an analytic estimate for the change in angular momentum of a cluster due to an impulsive interaction with a passing GMC, and verify this expectation by performing $N$-body simulations over a range of encounter parameters using REBOUND. For highly energetic encounters, significant angular momentum can be transferred, but the stars that receive the most angular momentum are ejected, leaving the cluster remnant with negligible net rotation. Even when considering a random walk of many GMC-cluster encounters, the integrated effects of these interactions cannot explain observations of dynamically old rotating open clusters. However, we find that within $\sim 5$ Myr post-encounter, some disrupted clusters could be confused as rotating clusters while their stars are still dispersing. Using the local density of GMCs, we estimate that up to $\approx 1\%$ of open clusters in the Milky Way may carry this faux-rotation signal.

papers.title: Nonlinear Tides of Binary Neutron Stars
papers.abstract: Nonlinear tides couple stellar oscillations and reshape the gravitational wave (GW) signal from inspiralling binaries. We present hydrodynamic simulations of nonlinear tides in inspiralling neutron-star binaries and, within a mode-coupling model, derive a semi-analytic quadrupolar fundamental mode-frequency shift through second order in the tidal strength. The two approaches agree in the perturbative regime, but diverge at stronger tidal fields, where perturbation theory breaks down. In the late inspiral, nonlinear tides reduce the fundamental-mode frequency by ${\sim}10\%$ for equal-mass binaries and add a GW phase shift of $\mathcal{O}(1)$ radian beyond the linear tidal response. These effects make nonlinear tides a promising target for next-generation GW detectors.

papers.title: A Fast and Memory-Efficient Algorithm for Searching Faint Moving Objects using Synthetic Tracking
papers.abstract: Detecting unknown faint moving objects using optical imaging is challenging. Long exposure times are infeasible for such targets, as the resulting image streaking causes a loss of signal-to-noise ratio due to energy dispersal across multiple pixels. To address this, synthetic tracking, a track-before-detect method, replaces long exposures with many short exposures, integrating them in post-processing to recover the moving signal. Enabled by modern CMOS detectors with fast readout and low read noise, this technique synthesizes telescope tracking by searching over a grid of velocities. However, the conventional brute-force implementation imposes a significant computational burden: integrating N_f frames of size (N_x,N_y) requires O(N_x N_y N_f^3) operations. This cost becomes prohibitive for megapixel-scale frames with N_f~100. Although dynamic programming can reduce the computational complexity by a factor of N_f, it requires a prohibitive memory of O(N_x N_y N_f^2), unsuitable for large-format detectors. This article presents a novel algorithm to achieve the computational efficiency of dynamic programming while maintaining a memory footprint of just O(N_x N_y N_f) by slightly approximating the computation of frame shifts for alignment. By expressing the shift as a sum of terms proportional to the digits frame index in binary and rounding up each of these terms, frames can be integrated efficiently by hierarchically adding intermediate sums that are shared across different velocities with the same higher bits in binary. The approximation only introduces a small tracking error that increases logarithmically with the number of frames. This advancement enables synthetic tracking to be executed with high energy efficiency, making it practical for deployment on standard workstations rather than requiring high-performance computing infrastructure such as GPU servers or CPU clusters.

papers.title: The UKIRT M33 Monitoring Project - VII. A 15-year K-band photometric catalogue of long-period variable stars in the central kiloparsec of M33
papers.abstract: We present a homogenised K-band photometric catalogue for the central ${\approx}12$ arcmin$^2$ (${\approx}0.9$ kpc$^2$) of the Triangulum spiral galaxy M33, combining four independent PSF-based near-infrared datasets obtained with UKIRT between 2003 and 2018. These comprise the 2003-2007 UIST multi-epoch monitoring survey, the 2005 UFTI K-band mosaic (for which we present new PSF photometry), new WFCAM PSF reductions for the four central tiles, and a single K-band epoch from the 2018 UKIRT Hemisphere Survey (UHS DR3). Cross-matching all four catalogues and retaining stars detected in at least two of them yields 847 unique stars comprising 21,085 valid K-band measurements spanning a baseline of 15.11 yr. Photometric homogenisation onto the 2MASS/Vega system via 82 low-scatter calibration stars removes systematic inter-dataset offsets of up to 0.22 mag. Of the 847 monitored stars, 771 (91 per cent) are classified as variable ($σ_{\rm rms} > 0.10$ mag), including 385 high-amplitude variables ($A_K \geq 1.0$ mag): prime Mira-type long-period variable candidates for period determination. Cross-matching with archival Spitzer IRAC photometry yields 156 matched stars, of which 120 satisfy $\langle K\rangle - [3.6] > 0.5$ mag, identifying dust-enshrouded AGB candidates inaccessible to all-sky optical surveys. This catalogue constitutes the most extensive near-infrared photometric baseline assembled for AGB stars in any spiral galaxy beyond the Milky Way, providing the photometric foundation for the period-luminosity analysis and star-formation-history reconstruction in the companion Paper VIII. The full catalogue is available at the Centre de Données astronomiques de Strasbourg (CDS).

papers.title: How common are extreme scattering events?: First large sample from the ASKAP VAST survey
papers.abstract: Compact radio sources are occasionally observed to undergo extreme scattering events (ESEs): large, chromatic flux-density variations, often by more than a factor of two, over a few months. These were interpreted to be a smooth plasma lensing phenomenon due to AU-scale structures in the ISM. Although ESEs were discovered decades ago, observationally, only a few tens of ESEs have been reported, often from individual sources monitored at very high cadences. As such, the nature of the plasma lenses generating such events remains elusive. In this article, we present the most comprehensive sample of ESEs to date, using the ASKAP Variables and Slow Transients (VAST) survey. We report the discovery of a three-tier sample --- 72 sources that show promising ESE events (gold), 76 sources that are likely ESE-exhibiting (silver), and an additional 88 sources where ESE events are one plausible explanation (bronze). We show that the light curves demonstrate varied morphologies, which can be interpreted in terms of the source size and the strength of the lens in the paradigm of a simple one-dimensional Gaussian lens model. The spatial distribution of ESEs shows an appreciable excess in the direction of the Galactic center and along the Galactic loops. Using this sample, we infer an overall rate of 0.012 such events per year per deg^2 (or 0.006 events per source per year) for our (gold+silver) sample, for sources with mean flux density above 5 mJy at 888 MHz (0.01% of all isolated point sources detected in VAST).

papers.title: Evidence for a nova super-remnant surrounding the recurrent nova V745 Scorpii using eROSITA
papers.abstract: Nova super-remnants (NSRs) are vast shell-like structures encompassing recurrent novae (RNe), created through the excavation of large amounts of local interstellar medium by repeated nova eruptions. Simulations predict that such NSRs should surround all novae. Indeed, NSRs have now been discovered around the Galactic RNe KT Eridani, RS Ophiuchi and T Coronae Borealis, and the Large Magellanic Cloud RN LMCN 1971-08a, to place alongside the prototypical NSR in M31, associated with the extreme RN, M31N 2008-12a. Highly energetic novae ejecta impacting the inner boundary of the NSR shell alongside inter-ejecta shocks are predicted to generate high levels of X-ray emission in the form of an extended shell-like structure. A search for X-ray emission from a present NSR surrounding the Galactic RN, V745 Scorpii, using observations from the extended Roentgen Survey with an Imaging Telescope Array (eROSITA) on board Spektrum-Roentgen-Gamma (Spektr-RG, SRG) led to the identification of a shell coincident with the nova. Based on (i) the structure being aligned with the location of the central nova; (ii) its size being consistent with the sizes of other known NSRs; (iii) the similarity between the emission radial profiles of the X-ray structure and the confirmed NSR around M31N 2008-12a; (vi) the presence of a corresponding infrared cavity; (v) the resemblance of the radial profile of the synthetic X-ray ring derived from a modelled NSR structure with the radial profile of the observed ring; and (vi) the lack of other sources capable of creating such a large structure, we propose this X-ray structure to be another Galactic NSR to be uncovered, and the first NSR to be captured through its X-ray emission.

papers.title: The First Deep Learning all-sky List of Fermi-LAT Gamma-ray Sources
papers.abstract: Aims: We develop a deep-learning-based pipeline to construct a list of γ-ray sources and to quantitatively assess the impact of background uncertainties on source detection and characterization. This work extends and enhances the existing AutoSource-ID algorithm, previously adopted on optical observations, for applications on γ-ray data. Methods: Source detection was performed through image segmentation using a U-Net architecture, while dedicated deep neural networks (DNNs) were employed for source localization, flux estimation, and the classification of detected sources as either genuine or spurious. The training data were generated from Monte Carlo simulations based on 10 years of Fermi-LAT observations. Results: We present the first Fermi-LAT γ-ray all-sky source list derived using a deep-learning-based method (1FDL), containing more than 3800 sources with estimated positions, fluxes, and probability scores that quantify the likelihood of each detection being genuine or spurious. We further evaluated the robustness of the pipeline against variations in the interstellar emission model (IEM) and compared the resulting source list with the 4FGL-DR2 catalog. Conclusion: We find that the our deep-learning-based approach achieves performance comparable to, or better than, the likelihood-based methods employed in the standard Fermi-LAT catalog pipeline when tested against changes in the IEM. The 1FDL source list is broadly consistent with the Fermi-LAT 4FGL-DR2 catalog obtained over the same 10-year observational period, including a few new sources confirmed in the recent Fermi-LAT 16-year source list (FL16Y). These results demonstrate the potential of DNN methods for the detection and characterization of γ-ray sources and provide a foundation for their application in future high-energy astrophysical analyses.

papers.title: Coherent Radio Emission from Flux Rope Mergers in 3D Relativistic Reconnection
papers.abstract: Coherent emission from merging plasmoids in relativistic reconnection is the leading model for radio emission originating in the outer magnetosphere of pulsars such as the Crab, and a candidate emission mechanism for fast radio bursts. This process has only been studied in 2D, and whether it survives in 3D, where the dynamics of structures in the reconnection layer can differ substantially, is still an open question. Here we present the first study of coherent wave generation from flux rope mergers in 3D relativistic reconnection. We use particle-in-cell simulations of relativistic reconnection with outflow boundary conditions and guide fields $B_g/B_0 = \{0,0.1,0.3\}$, and measure the efficiency $η$ with which inflowing magnetic energy is converted into escaping coherent waves. We find $η\sim 7\times10^{-4}$ without a guide field, a factor of a few below 2D results, and $η\sim(1\text{-}2) \times10^{-3}$ at moderate guide fields, comparable to 2D with no guide field. We propose a physical picture for why the efficiency remains comparable to 2D, based on how reconnected field is transported away from the diffusion regions. The escaping waves are linearly polarized, with a polarization angle set by the direction of the upstream field. In the presence of a guide field, waves escaping from opposite sides of the reconnection layer therefore differ in polarization angle by $ \sim 2\arctan(B_g/B_0)$. Our results support relativistic magnetic reconnection as the origin of coherent radio emission from Crab-like pulsars, and strengthen its case as a potential emission mechanism for fast radio bursts.

papers.title: Self lensing in BH-NS binaries as progenitors for periodically repeating Fast Radio Bursts
papers.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are bright extragalactic transients whose origin remains uncertain. The discovery of repeating FRBs, some with cyclic activity windows, opens new prospects for testing their progenitors. Neutron stars (NSs) are strong candidates, as they naturally emit radio pulses with temporal and spectral properties resembling those of FRBs, an interpretation reinforced by the detection of an FRB-like burst from the Galactic magnetar SGR 1935+2154. Nevertheless, the pulse energy of typical radio-emitting NSs remains several orders of magnitude below that of even the faintest observed FRBs. We explore a binary system in which a NS orbits a black hole (BH), so that NS radio pulses are gravitationally amplified through self-lensing, producing characteristic signatures in the energy distribution, activity windows, and waiting times that can be contrasted with observations. We implement a simple NS-BH binary model with a circular orbit undergoing Lense-Thirring precession, and compute how the pulses are lensed along the orbit, including pulse splitting and time delays. Pure Keplerian orbits produce activity windows several orders of magnitude shorter than those of periodic FRBs. Post-Keplerian orbits with Lense-Thirring precession are more promising, yielding windows of a few to tens of days. Lensing transforms an intrinsic log-normal NS pulse-energy distribution, producing a high-energy power-law tail spanning up to four orders of magnitude. Interpreting the observed millisecond waiting times between consecutive bursts as lensing-induced image delays, we infer BH masses of 10^3-10^4 solar masses, in the intermediate-mass (IMBH) range. However, the amplification in our model is insufficient to bridge the energy gap between Galactic magnetar radio pulses and FRBs. Moreover, the non-detection of NS-IMBH systems suggests a low abundance, so this channel is likely rare.

papers.title: FLITS: an interactive, reproducible workbench for fast radio burst analysis
papers.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are brief flashes of radio emission whose time, frequency, and polarization structure constrain their sources and propagation environments. FLITS (Fast-Look Interactive Transient Suite) is an open-source Python package with a browser interface for analysing detected bursts. It combines data inspection, interference mitigation, measurement, and modelling, including fits of the fitburst burst model, in a shared session, and reads SIGPROC filterbank, PSRFITS, and CHIME/FRB HDF5 data. The same routines measure larger samples from the command line and flag bursts whose automatic selections need checking. Trial dispersion measures can be scored by signal-to-noise, by burst structure, or with a smoothed-structure metric that also reports the range of dispersion measures consistent with the best one. Portable session files retain the selected data regions, excluded channels, calibration inputs, available results, input-data checksum, and software provenance, and supported measurements can be replayed from the command line and compared with their saved values. Uncertainty labels identify missing calibration information. A public reference workflow provides downloadable data and numerical checks.

papers.title: Topological Centrality in Gaia Open Clusters
papers.abstract: Open clusters exhibit diverse spatial structures that provide insight into their formation and dynamical evolution. We investigate the relationship between stellar mass segregation, network topology, and dynamical age in 871 dynamically unevolved open clusters ($τ= t/t_{\rm rh} \leq 1$) from Gaia-based catalogs. We construct three-dimensional k-nearest-neighbor graphs and measure Degree Centrality (DC), Closeness Centrality (CL), and Betweenness Centrality (BC). For each measure, we define a network-based mass segregation ratio (MSR) by comparing the mean centrality of the most massive stars with that of all cluster members. We test the stability of these measures across connectivity parameters $k=5$--20 and compare them with the classical 3D MSR, $Λ_{\rm MSR,3D}$, and dynamical age. All three network ratios show positive correlations with $Λ_{\rm MSR,3D}$, strongest for closeness centrality, while their correlations with dynamical age are weak. These results demonstrate that network analysis provides a complementary approach to studying stellar structure and mass segregation in open clusters.

papers.title: Excitation and Destruction of Small Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons by the Luminous Seyfert Nucleus of NGC 4151
papers.abstract: We present a spatially-resolved detection of $3.3\,\mathrm{μm}$ emission from polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) within the circumnuclear ${\sim}200\,\mathrm{pc}$ of the archetypal Seyfert galaxy NGC 4151, using new JWST NIRSpec/IFU spectroscopy. PAHs are detected down to the innermost $50\,\mathrm{pc}$, though it is likely that PAHs also exist at smaller radii, as PAH detections closer than this seem to be limited by continuum dilution. This is contrary to expectations that PAH grains, especially the smallest grains that carry the $3.3\,\mathrm{μm}$ feature, could not survive near an active galactic nucleus (AGN). Furthermore, the surface brightness of PAH emission increases as radius from the nucleus decreases. We interpret this as evidence that the AGN supplies energy for PAH excitation by driving ultraviolet emission in nearby H and $\mathrm{H_2}$ gas. We do not detect PAH emission within the narrow line region (NLR) that hosts highly ionized and outflowing gas, suggesting that the AGN may also destroy PAHs in these regions, depending on geometry. Together, these results show that an AGN has a complex, multifaceted role in the life cycle of PAHs and in PAH excitation.

papers.title: When Scatter Plots Hide the Data: Diagnosing Ties and Choosing the Right Display in R
papers.abstract: Scatter plots draw one mark per observation, so observations that share a location are hidden. In a two-item Likert survey of 2,757 respondents, 98.7% of the data lie under other points and the plot shows only 36 dots. The density-distribution sunflower plot of Dupont and Plummer addresses this by drawing raw points in sparse regions and sunflowers, whose petals count observations, in dense ones. It is not available in R, and its single petal weight for dense cells fails when cell counts span more than an order of magnitude: small dense cells collapse to one petal, and the count a reader decodes can be wrong by 150% or more. We propose geometric petal tiers, in which each cell uses the smallest weight among 1, b, b2, . . . observations per petal that keeps its flower within P petals. Every flower then has between about P/b and P petals, and the relative error of every decoded count is below b/(2P), 17.9% at the defaults b = 5 and P = 14. We also define tie diagnostics and decision rules that use them to choose between an ordinary scatter plot, jitter or transparency, a classic sunflower plot and geometric tiers. Both are implemented in the ggplot2 extension ggsunflower. We illustrate the methods on survey, automotive, historical and large commercial data, and in a simulation over 35 conditions geometric tiers keep the worst-cell error at or below 14% where a single weight reaches a median of 251%.

papers.title: ASKAP Discovery of a Giant Odd Radio Circle at $z=0.15$
papers.abstract: Odd radio circles (ORCs) are a recently recognized class of faint, roughly circular diffuse radio sources, typically a few hundred kiloparsecs across, whose origin is still debated. We report the serendipitous discovery of a giant ORC, ORC~J1928$-$5056, in 856~MHz continuum data from the ASKAP observations. The emission forms a single, mildly elliptical structure $4^{\prime}$ across, corresponding to $0.63$~Mpc at the redshift $z=0.1507$ of the central galaxy LEDA~140850, the brightest cluster galaxy of Abell~3639, which makes it one of the largest single ORCs known. After subtracting the radio nucleus associated with the host galaxy, the ORC has a flux density of 73~mJy integrated within an area of $\sim 12$~arcmin$^2$, i.e.\ a mean surface brightness of only $1.7$~$μ$Jy~arcsec$^{-2}$, and a rest-frame luminosity of $L_{1.4}=2\times10^{24}$~W~Hz$^{-1}$, comparable to those of the most luminous ORCs. Including its nucleus, the system reaches $L_{1.4}=6.6\times10^{24}$~W~Hz$^{-1}$, higher than that of any other ORC reported so far. The host is a massive ($M_{\ast}\sim10^{11}\,M_{\odot}$), passive elliptical galaxy with negligible star formation. It contains an AGN jet with a power-law spectrum of index $α=-0.877\pm0.089$ between 856 and 1656~MHz. Finally, we discuss the implications for ORC formation models and the observations needed to establish the nature of this system.

papers.title: Calculation of distant retrograde orbits and their use in space weather forecasting
papers.abstract: There is current renewed interest in using Sun-Earth distant retrograde orbits (DROs) for a space weather forecasting mission, which would temporarily place spacecraft at a position near the Sun-Earth line, but closer to the Sun than the L1 point (such as the ESA HENON mission and ESA SHIELD concept). With in situ observations of the magnetic field on a DRO, the southward ($B_z < 0$) magnetic field of interplanetary coronal mass ejections (ICMEs), which is not routinely accessible remotely, could be measured several hours in advance. This $B_z < 0$ field is a decisive factor for forecasting geomagnetic storm intensity. We present an analysis of DROs at different sub-L1 distances for their efficacy for a space weather forecasting mission. An open-source numerical framework to generate DRO trajectories is presented. Our pre-calculated orbits in Heliocentric Earth Ecliptic coordinates can be introduced into numerical or empirical simulations of the ambient solar wind and ICMEs. We then analyze the corresponding forecast lead times, the resulting observational gaps depending on the number of spacecraft and distance of a DRO, and the "cone of acceptance" of the maximum longitudinal separation of a spacecraft to the Sun-Earth line. We define different domains regarding radial evolution and longitudinal CME structure, and show the historical coverage of sub-L1 ICME observations with our ICMECAT catalog. An optimal mission configuration can be selected based on the characteristics of DROs presented here, depending on the requirements of such a mission deemed acceptable with respect to results on CME evolution and coherence.

papers.title: Reconstruction of very inclined air showers with radio data and application to the first GRANDProto300 cosmic-ray candidates
papers.abstract: Radio detection of very inclined extensive air showers (EAS) offers a promising way to study ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) and neutrinos above $10^{17}$ eV. We present a method to reconstruct the arrival direction and energy of EAS with zenith angles above $60^\circ$, applicable in principle to upward-going neutrino-induced showers. The approach combines a point-source-like description of the radio wavefront with the Angular Distribution Function (ADF), a phenomenological model describing the angular pattern of electric field amplitudes in the 50-200 MHz band. On realistic cosmic-ray simulations, we achieve better than $0.07^\circ$ resolution on arrival direction and ~15\% on primary energy. Applied directly to voltage traces, this method allows efficient cosmic-ray selection with accurate direction reconstruction and first-order energy estimation. We illustrate the method on the first cosmic-ray candidates detected by the GRANDProto300 prototype of GRAND, validating its detection principle and paving the way for high-precision neutrino searches.

papers.title: Testing Pre-main-sequence Evolutionary Models with Gaia and SPHEREx Observations of Canis Major North
papers.abstract: Pre-main-sequence (PMS) evolutionary models can assign different ages across stellar mass within the same population. We use joint Gaia and SPHEREx spectral energy distributions to infer effective temperatures, radii, and luminosities for members of Canis Major North (CMaN), a nearby association with independent lithium and kinematic age constraints near 23 Myr. The SPHEREx fluxes agree with 2MASS and WISE photometry to 3--6\%, and we anchor the absolute flux scale to Gaia, 2MASS, and WISE. Using the revised temperatures, we obtain a lithium age of $22.4^{+2.8}_{-1.5}$ Myr. For a 29-star PMS sample, population-wide HR-diagram fits yield $20.5^{+1.5}_{-1.4}$ Myr for unspotted SPOTS models, consistent with the external constraints, $18.4^{+1.4}_{-1.3}$ and $18.7^{+1.3}_{-1.2}$ Myr for the Feiden nonmagnetic and BHAC15 models, and substantially older ages of $32.2^{+2.3}_{-2.1}$ and $55^{+5}_{-5}$ Myr for the Feiden magnetic and PARSEC models. No grid returns a temperature-independent age. The Feiden, SPOTS, and BHAC15 models assign older ages to stars above $4000$ K, whereas PARSEC assigns increasingly older ages toward lower temperatures. The intrinsic luminosity dispersion is also mass dependent, approximately $0.14$ dex below $3450$ K but $0.05$ dex at intermediate temperatures. At a fixed age of 23.0 Myr, a single SPOTS filling factor cannot reproduce the width of the low-temperature sequence, whereas the empirical filling-factor distribution of young stars overpredicts it. Spotted isochrones can enclose every cool member only at ages of 37--50 Myr, inconsistent with the lithium and kinematic ages.

papers.title: Propulsion Systems for a Starshade Rendezvous Mission with the Habitable World Observatory
papers.abstract: We assess how propulsion and operational constraints affect exo-Earth characterization with a starshade rendezvous mission for a Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO)-like telescope at Sun-Earth L2. Using end-to-end Monte Carlo simulations with EXOSIMS, we model a 60 m starshade for visible-band spectroscopy (500-1000 nm) and a 35 m starshade for near-ultraviolet characterization (250-550 nm). For the 60 m design, we compare AEPS Hall, NEXT ion, and Starlink-class Hall thrusters and examine sensitivity to propellant capacity, the fraction of each retargeting slew spent accelerating and decelerating, and on-orbit refueling. With 1000-3000 kg of initial propellant and no refueling, NEXT provides the highest characterization yield: 9-13% more characterizations than AEPS and 13-16% more than the Starlink-class option. Its higher specific impulse enables more retargeting slews per kilogram of propellant. With refueling, yields converge across thruster choices to about 120 cumulative characterizations over 10 years, while propulsion choice mainly affects the number of refueling events. For the 35 m starshade with AEPS, yields are less sensitive to fuel and are dominated by mission duration and geometric accessibility. Increasing the minimum solar keepout angle from 40 to 50 degrees has little effect on yield; increases from 50 to 65 degrees have a modest effect, while angles above 65 degrees rapidly reduce yield, with severe degradation near 80 degrees. These results distinguish fuel-limited and time- or keepout-limited regimes and guide propulsion selection, tank sizing, refueling policy, and keepout constraints for HWO starshade missions.

papers.title: How particle physics stops ultra-relativistic bubbles and shapes their gravitational waves
papers.abstract: The gravitational-wave spectrum produced by ultra-relativistic bubbles in a first-order cosmological phase transition can be approximated in terms of their energy density as a function of bubble size. Bubble collisions and post-collision classical evolution negligibly change it. The dominant energy loss is particle scattering, often in the Landau--Pomeranchuk--Migdal regime. So the GW spectrum depends on the particle-physics coupling (interpolating between the `envelope' and `bulk flow' limits), on the interaction type (gauge, Yukawa, scalar quartic, ...), and on whether particle number is conserved. Finally, we consider broken global symmetries, which give a mixture of `elastic' and `inelastic' collisions.

papers.title: ASTRA: An Autonomous Framework for Physics-Validated Analysis and Hypothesis Generation in Astrophysics
papers.abstract: We present ASTRA, an autonomous framework for physics-validated analysis and hypothesis generation in astrophysics without per-step human intervention. It integrates dimensional analysis, structural causal models, Bayesian evidence computation, and multi-wavelength data fusion in a single automated workflow. Five test cases on real observational data recover known results: Herschel filament scaling, Chandra Deep Field South cross-matching, SDSS galaxy correlations, Gaia causal inference, and Bayesian virial model selection. A sixth case runs unsupervised on synthetic galaxy data. The main sequence and mass-metallicity relation are recovered, and the outlier detector, with a false-discovery-rate threshold and no contamination parameter, recovers the blind injected fraction on ten sealed datasets (purity > 0.99) and flags nothing on the 3,000-galaxy sample. A knowledge-isolation ablation shows pattern detection and physical validation are invariant to removal of domain knowledge, which affects only interpretation. In a direct comparison, agentic-LLM and pure-ML baselines match the statistical fitting but not the physics-validation stage. They rarely derive the equilibrium benchmark, split evenly on the physical verdict, and adopt a supplied erroneous benchmark in all six trap runs, an astrophysics-specific fine-tuned model completes zero of six runs. On live SDSS DR16 data it flags 197 of 4,999 galaxies at a data-determined threshold, ranked extremes classifiable from withheld spectroscopy. These are recovery validations and capability demonstrations rather than discoveries, with hypothesis generation demonstrated qualitatively.

papers.title: Dynamical constraints on the companion mass from pulsar timing and cyclotron line confirmation in the SFXT IGR J16418-4532
papers.abstract: Supergiant Fast X-ray Transients (SFXTs) show extreme X-ray variability on timescales of minutes to hours, driven by accretion processes that remain poorly understood. IGR J16418-4532 is an intermediate SFXT with detected X-ray pulsations and a candidate cyclotron line, making it a key system for probing neutron-star accretion and magnetic fields in this class. We analysed a 148 ks NuSTAR observation and archival RXTE observations, using epoch folding to search for pulsations while correcting photon arrival times for a range of trial $a_x \sin i$ values, and performed phase-averaged spectroscopy with several continuum models. We detect coherent pulsations at $P_{\rm spin} = 1208.67 \pm 0.04$ s (NuSTAR) and $1209.4178 \pm 0.0084$ s (RXTE/PCA). The pulse detection depends clearly on the assumed projected semi-major axis and is most significant for $a_x \sin i = 55.1 \pm 3.5$ lt-s (NuSTAR) and $51.3 \pm 2.6$ lt-s (RXTE/PCA). Sliding-window pulse profiles show the orbital delay in the uncorrected data, which is fully removed after orbital correction. The inferred orbital parameters constrain the companion mass and radius to $\sim$12-18 $M_\odot$ and $\sim$13-16 $R_\odot$. This is the first constraint on the binary mass function of an SFXT obtained from the orbital motion of the neutron star. The spectrum shows a robust cyclotron absorption line at $\sim$50 keV, independent of the continuum model, implying $B \approx 5 \times 10^{12}$ G. Optimising pulse detection with trial $a_x \sin i$ corrections, rather than modelling pulse arrival-time delays, offers a route to dynamical mass measurements in other SFXTs whose variable pulse profiles limit conventional timing techniques.

papers.title: Protostellar Outflows at the EarliesT Stages (POETS) X. Preliminary statistics of 6.7 GHz masers near POETS sources
papers.abstract: So far, the POETS survey has focused on studying at high angular resolution the properties of both 22.2 GHz H2O masers and the radio continuum emission near young stellar objects (YSOs). Now, we want to add the information coming from another star formation tracer, the Class II 6.7 GHz CH3OH (methanol) maser, towards the same POETS targets. We seek to probe the existence of 6.7 GHz maser emission near POETS sources with high sensitivity observations and study their kinematic properties with respect to local radio continuum and 22.2 GHz maser emission at high angular and spectral resolutions. Within the POETS survey, we used the Very Large Array (VLA) in the A configuration, operating at high spectral resolution (0.1 km/s) and achieving a sensitivity of a few mJy/beam per channel map, in order to (i) probe the emission from methanol gas in the 6.7 GHz maser transition and (ii) trace its absolute spatial distribution and local standard of rest velocity. We present a preliminary analysis of 6.7 GHz CH3OH maser emission toward a subsample of the POETS survey (22 fields observed so far), 60 % of which show detection above a brightness temperature threshold of 10^7 K. Five sources among this subsample are new detections. We draw a 6.7 GHz maser brightness function by studying the distribution of the intrinsic luminosity of the maser population and predict that more than 30 % of the whole population is undetected at typical interferometric sensitivities of a few 10 mJy/beam. We confirm that 6.7 GHz masers arise close to the young star they are associated with and quantify that, on average, 90 % of them are distributed within radii of 3000 au only. Furthermore, we find a tight correlation between the 6.7 GHz maser luminosity coming from a given source and the local free-free emission, suggesting that the radio continuum provides the dominant source of seed photons amplified by the methanol gas.

papers.title: Axionic Quintessence in Heterotic String Theory
papers.abstract: We investigate axionic quintessence in heterotic string compactifications. Starting from the ten-dimensional theory, we derive the four-dimensional axion effective action, including gauge couplings and non-perturbative potentials, and identify the curvature terms that can correct it. We examine the geometric requirements for ultralight axions generated by exponentially suppressed worldsheet instantons, finding significant restrictions through an exploratory scan of toric Calabi-Yau hypersurfaces. In an illustrative K3-fibred setup, the minimal benchmark also encounters a tension with the positivity of the one-loop corrected gauge kinetic functions. Aligned worldsheet-instanton contributions provide a way to alleviate this tension and yield an ultralight axion with a phenomenologically relevant decay constant. Our analysis also identifies lower-action instantons whose contributions must be controlled to preserve the ultralight axion. We then study the resulting class of quintessence potentials and qualitatively compare their late-time cosmological solutions with observationally preferred ranges.

papers.title: Semi-agnostic inspiral modeling: the massless scalar case at leading post-Newtonian order
papers.abstract: We introduce a semi-agnostic modeling framework for black hole binary inspirals beyond general relativity that fixes the field content without selecting a particular theory. We expand in the post-Newtonian order and in powers of $l/L$, where $l$ is the characteristic length-scale that controls deviations from General Relativity and $L$ is the characteristic length-scale of the system. We focus on the case of a massless scalar field coupled with the metric, at leading post-Newtonian order. Taking into account the scaling with $l/L$ of both the interaction terms and the quantities that characterise the sources, we find that the inspiral can be described in terms of a small number of universal parameters. Such a parametrisation is suitable for obtaining combined bounds from multiple sources and performing searches for specific fields.

papers.title: Interaction of Strong X-mode Waves with Magnetized Pair Plasmas
papers.abstract: The interaction of strong ($a_0>1$), superluminal X-mode electromagnetic waves with magnetized pair plasma falls into two regimes set by $\varepsilon_{\rm B}\equiv a_0ω_{\rm B}/ω_0$, the ratio of the wave strength parameter to its frequency, in units of cyclotron frequency. For $\varepsilon_{\rm B}<1$ the wave propagates until induced scattering disrupts it. Using analytical theory and kinetic simulations, we show that the background magnetic field introduces a restoring frequency $Ω_{\rm B}$ to scattering; when $Ω_{\rm B}$ exceeds the scattering rate, the unattenuated length grows from $\simeq\varepsilon_{\rm p}^{-2/3}$ to $\simeq\varepsilon_{\rm B}^{1/2}/\varepsilon_{\rm p}$ wavelengths ($\varepsilon_{\rm p}\equiv a_0ω_{\rm p}/ω_0$; $ω_{\rm p}$ is the plasma frequency). When $a_0^2>\varepsilon_{\rm B}>1$, the plasma current is nonlinear, and the wave is damped while riding a motional electric field, so one half-cycle appears attenuated. This framework has implications for the duration of fast radio bursts and whether they can escape their surroundings.

papers.title: Tidal contributions to neutron star orbital precession around Sgr $A^*$
papers.abstract: We investigate tidal contributions to the orbital precession of neutron stars around the supermassive black hole Sgr A*, using stellar configurations described by the Tolman - Oppenheimer - Volkoff equations. We examine the dependence of tidal precession on stellar compactness, pericentre distance, and the quadrupolar tidal Love number $k_2$, and compare its magnitude with general relativistic orbital precession. The calculated tidal angular shift decreases strongly with increasing pericentre distance and, for the stellar configurations considered, with increasing compactness. Larger Love numbers enhance the tidal contribution. This behaviour reflects the strong dependence of tidal precession on the stellar-radius-to-pericentre-distance ratio, $(R/r_p)^5$. Despite the enhancement during closer encounters, the predicted tidal shifts remain extremely small, reaching approximately $3.5 \times 10^{-18},μas$ within the displayed parameter range. The ratio of tidal to general relativistic precession spans approximately $10^{-33}$ - $10^{-28}$, indicating that relativistic precession overwhelmingly dominates.
